issues.body: `already_refused` accepts the marker from any comment body, and `read_comments` returns comments without enforcing an author identity. The new `refuse` path now promotes that unauthenticated marker into census evidence: a PR author or drive-by commenter can paste `<!-- auto-mint-provenance:refusal:<reason> -->`, causing `refused_standing`/`standing_refusals` to increase and suppressing the real annotation. Thus the claimed stuck-population measurement is author-controlled rather than evidence written by the auto-minter. The new tests only provide body-only comment fixtures, so none would fail when an untrusted author forges the marker.
issues.fix_hint: Preserve and validate comment authorship in the evidence path. Count a marker as standing only when the comment was authored by the known bot/App identity that posts auto-mint annotations; treat missing or unexpected author metadata as non-standing or fail closed. Add adversarial tests where the identical marker is supplied by the PR author/another user and prove it neither increments the standing census nor suppresses the legitimate annotation, plus a positive trusted-author case.
issues.title: Standing-refusal evidence is forgeable by any commenter

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The refusal partition and pre-cap probing are arithmetically coherent, but the new standing-population evidence is not authenticated. Any commenter can forge the marker that `already_refused` treats as proof of a prior auto-minter annotation, so the census can suppress a needed annotation and report a fresh refusal as standing. Because this is the trust-plane evidence path underlying the change's marquee claim, it requires changes.
